package_info.package_versions: all published versions as of April 24th, 2023
package_info.why_malicious: The packages contain heavily obfuscated code that monkey-patches core JavaScript built-ins (sessionStorage.getItem, Array.prototype.includes, Array.prototype.filter, JSON.stringify) to introduce random, non-deterministic, and unpredictable behavior. This can break application logic, cause subtle bugs, and is a common tactic for hiding malicious or unwanted behavior. The obfuscation and modification of global objects without user consent or documentation is highly suspicious and violates user trust.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code monkey-patches sessionStorage.getItem to randomly (5% probability) reverse the string value returned, introducing non-deterministic behavior into session storage retrieval.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Modifying a global browser API to randomly alter its output is highly suspicious and can break application logic in unpredictable ways.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: sessionStorage.getItem is expected to reliably return the stored value; introducing random string reversal violates this expectation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, developers may monkey-patch for debugging or polyfilling, but never to introduce random corruption.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code monkey-patches Array.prototype.includes to always return false for arrays of odd length, regardless of actual content, causing unpredictable and incorrect inclusion checks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Altering a core array method to return incorrect results based on array length is deceptive and can silently break application logic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Array.prototype.includes should accurately check for element presence; this patch introduces false negatives.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case for this behavior.
key_indicators: Conditional logic unrelated to method purpose

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code monkey-patches Array.prototype.filter to randomly (10% probability) remove one element from the filtered result, but only on Sundays, introducing time-based and random corruption.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Randomly altering the output of a core array method based on the day of the week is highly deceptive and can cause subtle, hard-to-debug errors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Array.prototype.filter should return all elements matching the predicate; this patch introduces random data loss.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case for this behavior.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code monkey-patches JSON.stringify to randomly (10% probability) replace all uppercase 'I' characters with lowercase 'l' in the serialized output, corrupting JSON data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Randomly corrupting JSON output can break data interchange and cause subtle bugs, especially since the change is visually hard to spot.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: JSON.stringify should reliably serialize objects; this patch introduces random, silent data corruption.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case for this behavior.

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the package, triggering execution of index.js.
attack_chain.leads_to: Global JavaScript built-ins are monkey-patched with non-deterministic, corrupted behavior.

attack_chain.action: Application code using sessionStorage.getItem, Array.prototype.includes, Array.prototype.filter, or JSON.stringify receives unpredictable, incorrect, or corrupted results.
attack_chain.leads_to: Silent, hard-to-debug application errors and potential data corruption.

behavioral_signatures: Monkey-patching of global JavaScript built-ins (sessionStorage.getItem, Array.prototype.includes/filter, JSON.stringify)
Introduction of random or time-based logic into core methods
Obfuscated code in index.js or main entry point
file_indicators: index.js containing obfuscated or minified code
References to global objects and prototype methods in package entry point
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan for packages that monkey-patch global JavaScript objects or prototype methods, especially with obfuscated or minified code. Look for code that introduces random or time-based logic into built-in functions. Flag packages whose entry points contain such modifications, particularly if the package name mimics popular libraries (e.g., lodash).
